- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecasted values by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days post-spike.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >35.0), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a downward bias of 3–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; cap forecast range within ±2.5% of recent 7-day moving average.
- Model underestimates true price divergence in the 15–25 day horizon; adjust upward by 1–3% for days 15–25 if true outcome shows sustained upward trend.
- If true outcome exceeds 40.0 after 10+ days, model fails to capture momentum; increase forecasted value by 2–4% for days 10–20 to align with observed acceleration.
- Model ignores sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive (even slightly >0.00), increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to reflect market momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >38.0 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes below 38.0.
- Horizon-specific error: model underestimates 30-day true outcome by 3–5% on average; apply a 3–5% upward adjustment for final 5–7 days of forecast.
